title: Which distribution family?
description: Sort distributions, package tools and package formats into the four families the exam names.

items.why: Ubuntu is built on Debian and made by Canonical, so it belongs to the Debian family.
RHEL is the commercial product the Enterprise Linux family is named after.
Leap is the free community release that shares its core with SUSE Linux Enterprise.
Alpine is a small, security-minded distribution with musl, BusyBox and its own package manager. It forms a family of its own.
`apt` is the high-level package tool of Debian and Ubuntu. It fetches packages and their dependencies.
`dnf` is the high-level package tool of the Enterprise Linux family (Fedora, RHEL, AlmaLinux, Rocky Linux).
`zypper` is the package tool of openSUSE and SUSE Linux Enterprise.
`apk` is Alpine’s own package manager, and its packages are `.apk` files.
The official system for Raspberry Pi boards is based on Debian.
Fedora is the community distribution that tries new things first. RHEL is developed from it, and it is listed in the Enterprise Linux family.
Mint is a beginner-friendly desktop distribution based on Ubuntu and Debian, so it is a Debian-family member.
Rocky Linux is a free, community-driven distribution that aims to be compatible with RHEL.
SLE is SUSE’s commercial product, and openSUSE is its free community relative.
The `.deb` format is installed with `dpkg` and `apt` on Debian and Ubuntu.
CentOS Stream sits between Fedora and RHEL, where the next RHEL minor releases take shape.
AlmaLinux is a free, RHEL-compatible community distribution, like Rocky Linux.
Tumbleweed is openSUSE’s rolling release with the newest software, and it uses `zypper` like Leap.
`dpkg` installs a single `.deb` file you already have. It does not fetch dependencies, which is why `apt` is used on top.
